Hugging Face Transformers 5.19.0 | Freedom.Tech

 Release Tue, Oct 6, 2026 6 min read 

# Hugging Face Transformers 5.19.0

At a glance

Transformers 5.19.0 adds EmbeddingGemma2 multimodal model, fixes MoE router logits output, enables expert parallelism without TP size constraints, and fixes quantized cache handling

Original release notes

## Release v5.19.0

## New Model additions

### EmbeddingGemma2

EmbeddingGemma 2 is a multimodal embedding model from Google built on the Gemma 4 architecture. It encodes text, images, audio, and video, individually or combined in one input, into a shared 768-dimensional vector space for cross-modal retrieval, semantic similarity, clustering, and classification. It uses Matryoshka Representation Learning, so embeddings can be truncated to 512, 256, or 128 dimensions. It also offers configurable visual and video token budgets, and unused vision or audio towers can be disabled at load time to save memory.

Links: Documentation

- Smthn smthn (#49364) by @vasqu in #49364

## Breaking changes

All MoE models whose routers compute logits now return them when `output_router_logits=True`, following the Qwen3-MoE pattern (a `router_logits` recorder on the base model, `MoeModelOutputWithPast` from the backbone, and a MoE causal LM output from the head), so code that relied on the previous outputs or their absence should read the router logits from these output classes.

- Return router logits from every MoE model that computes them (#48920) by @qgallouedec

`Owlv2ForObjectDetection.embed_image_query` now selects the query box with the highest objectness score, as in the original OWLv2 notebook, instead of the OWL-ViT heuristic, so image-guided query embeddings and detections may differ from earlier releases.

- Select the OWLv2 image query by objectness (#49200) by @qgallouedec

The `"paged|"` prefix for SDPA and flash attention implementations is deprecated, so users should set the regular attention implementation (e.g. `sdpa` or `flash_attention_2`) for continuous batching instead of `paged|sdpa` or `paged|flash_attention_2`.

- Attention Deprecate "paged|" prefix for SDPA and flash (#49112) by @remi-or

The regular flash and SDPA attention functions (`flash_attention.py`, `sdpa_attention.py`) now support continuous batching directly, and `"paged|..."` implementations for these are redirected to them, while eager still requires the `"paged|eager"` prefix.

- Attention Make regular attention support CB (#49101) by @remi-or

In continuous batching, the cache update for the index-based and block-table paths is now fused into a single call, which slightly changes the cache update function's behavior and affects any custom code that calls the separate update paths.

- [CB] Fuse update for index and block table path (#49088) by @remi-or

Continuous batching internals changed in preparation for removing `"paged"`: `max

- [CB] Little fixes before removing "paged" (#49069) by @remi-or

## Parallelization

Expert parallelism gains a token-dispatch implementation, selected via the new `ep_dispatch_experts` plan rule and now the default for Qwen3 MoE and Mellum, which removes the requirement that EP size equal TP size. The `Trainer` was also adapted to work with expert parallelism, and the docs now note that PEFT adapters support tensor parallelism. A CI-related fix for pipeline-parallel chart2table inference was also included.

- [`distributed`]: adapt Trainer to work Expert Parallel (#48873) by @3outeille in [#48873]
- [`distributed`] Add expert-parallel token dispatch, default for Qwen3 MoE (#48865) by @3outeille in [#48865]
- Fix pp chart2table inference (#49225) by @zucchini-nlp in [#49225]
- [docs] TP for PEFT adapters (#49060) by @stevhliu in [#49060]

## Cache

This release fixes quantized cache handling: `generate` no longer mutates the user's `cache_config`, and `QuantizedLayer.reorder_cache` is repaired. It also adds per-layer cache configuration, so `DynamicCache` and `StaticCache` initialize e

results.text:
Transformers 5.19: EmbeddingGemma 2 and MoE Routing

Runtime 7 Oct 2026

# Transformers 5.19 adds EmbeddingGemma 2 and expands MoE expert parallelism

Hugging Face’s October 6 release adds Google’s multimodal EmbeddingGemma 2 architecture, makes token-dispatch expert parallelism the default for Qwen3 MoE and Mellum, and repairs quantized-cache behavior.

Open Model Weights published 7 Oct 2026 Primary source Hugging Face Transformers Source published 2026-10-06

Hugging Face has released Transformers 5.19.0 with changes that matter to both open-weight model support and large-model deployment. The headline model addition is EmbeddingGemma 2, a Google multimodal embedding architecture built on Gemma 4. According to the release notes, it can encode text, images, audio and video into a shared 768-dimensional space and uses Matryoshka Representation Learning so applications can truncate embeddings to 512, 256 or 128 dimensions. The implementation also exposes configurable visual and video token budgets and allows unused vision or audio towers to be disabled at load time.

The release also changes how mixture-of-experts models are parallelized. Transformers now includes an expert-parallel token-dispatch implementation and makes it the default for Qwen3 MoE and Mellum. Hugging Face says this removes the earlier requirement that expert-parallel size match tensor-parallel size. Trainer support has also been adapted for expert parallelism, while the documentation now covers tensor parallelism with PEFT adapters. Separately, MoE models that compute router logits now expose them through a more consistent output path when requested.

Cache handling receives another set of deployment-relevant fixes. Version 5.19.0 repairs quantized-cache behavior, prevents generate from mutating a user-supplied cache configuration and adds per-layer cache configuration for heterogeneous models. For Open Model Weights, these are runtime and architecture-support facts: they can strengthen compatibility evidence where the release explicitly names a family, but they should not alter checkpoint, license or weight-artifact fields without direct repository evidence.

## What this changes for the evidence layer

Runtime and architecture-support evidence. The release can support compatibility signals for model families it explicitly names, but it does not by itself verify a checkpoint, weight list, license or publisher field. EmbeddingGemma 2 should only enter the canonical registry after its own repository artifacts and license evidence are checked.

## Hugging Face Transformers

This brief is based on the cited primary source. Performance, benchmark and comparative claims remain attributed unless Open Model Weights publishes an independent measurement.

KEY FACTS

- Transformers v5.19.0 was released on October 6 and adds EmbeddingGemma 2, a multimodal embedding architecture built on Gemma 4.
- The release describes a shared 768-dimensional embedding space for text, images, audio and video, with Matryoshka truncation to 512, 256 or 128 dimensions.
- Expert-parallel token dispatch becomes the default plan for Qwen3 MoE and Mellum, while quantized-cache handling and per-layer cache configuration are also updated.

results.text:
Hugging Face Transformers 5.18.0 | Freedom.Tech

 Release Wed, Sep 30, 2026 8 min read 

# Hugging Face Transformers 5.18.0

At a glance

Transformers 5.18.0 adds Nemotron 3 Diarization for speaker identification, NemotronH Omni for multimodal reasoning, HyperCLOVAX Vision V2, and GTE embeddings

Original release notes

## New Model additions

### Nemotron 3 Diarization

Nemotron 3 Diarization is an open-weight streaming speaker diarization model designed to determine "who spoke when" in real-world audio. It supports both streaming and offline inference, handles up to eight speakers, and orders speaker outputs by each speaker's first arrival in the input audio.

The model uses the Arrival-Order Speaker Cache (AOSC) 1 and FIFO queue introduced for Streaming Sortformer 1, 2. A single checkpoint supports configurable latency profiles, from an 80 ms input buffer to a 30.4 s offline-style buffer, and configurable output frame resolution in multiples of 10 ms. With chunked inference, the maximum audio duration is not limited.

Links: Documentation

- Add Nemotron3Diarization (#49056) by @eustlb in #49056

### NemotronH Omni

NemotronH Omni is a multimodal reasoning model from NVIDIA that pairs the NemotronH hybrid Mamba-Transformer language model with a RADIO vision encoder and an optional Parakeet-based sound encoder. Image (and video) patches are projected through a RADIO tower and a pixel-shuffle MLP into the language model's embedding space at the ` ` / ` ` context-token positions; audio clips are projected in the same way at ` ` positions. The result is a single autoregressive model that reasons jointly over text, images, video and sound.

Links: Documentation

- Add support for Nemotron Omni (#46509) by @meatybobby in #46509

### HyperCLOVAX Vision V2

HyperCLOVAX Vision V2 is a multimodal vision-language model developed by NAVER. It combines the HyperClovaX language model backbone with a Qwen2.5-VL vision encoder. The model supports text, image, and video inputs and is capable of chain-of-thought reasoning via built-in thinking tokens (`... `).

Links: Documentation

- add HyperClovaX Vision (#44314) by @jp1924 in #44314

### GTE

GTE was proposed in mGTE: Generalized Long-Context Text Representation and Reranking Models for Multilingual Text Retrieval by Xin Zhang, Yanzhao Zhang, Dingkun Long, Wen Xie, Ziqi Dai, Jialong Tang, Huan Lin, Baosong Yang, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang, Meishan Zhang, Wenjie Li and Min Zhang.

GTE is a BERT-style bidirectional encoder that replaces absolute position embeddings with RoPE, uses a gated MLP, and applies layer normalization after each residual connection. The same architecture backs Alibaba's `gte-*-v1.5`, `gte-multilingual-*` and `gte-en-mlm-*` checkpoints as well as Snowflake's `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0`.

Links: Documentation

- model: Add GTE to Transformers (#48416) by @harshaljanjani in #48416

## Breaking changes

- [ROCm] gpt-oss: route FA3 to aiter-flash-attn, generate ROCm fixtures (#46837) by @Abdennacer-Badaoui
- Speed up detr image processing (#48066) by @guarin
- Remap indexers layer_type (#48974) by @Cyrilvallez
- [vLLM] Fix video token counting for Transformers backend video inputs (Part 1) (#48894) by @harshaljanjani

Transformers drops legacy data helpers, TRL rebuilds GOLD · Hugging Face · RepoJournal

 Oct 13, 2026 

# Transformers drops legacy data helpers, TRL rebuilds GOLD tests on real trainers 

 By RepoJournal · Filed 06:58 UTC on October 13, 2026 · About Hugging Face · Composed from the cited sources · methodology 

 

 10 people shipped this 

 SunMarc @SunMarc 2 cited albertvillanova @albertvillanova 2 cited Raymondlol @Raymondlol 1 cited archiep867-sys @archiep867-sys dangruiyuan @dangruiyuan guarin @guarin danieldk @danieldk ariG23498 @ariG23498 hf-kernels-bot @hf-kernels-bot Quentin Gallouédec @qgallouedec 

 A housekeeping day across the Hugging Face stack: Transformers removed years-deprecated GLUE/SQuAD/XNLI data helpers and stray cross-model imports, while TRL replaced stub-built GOLD trainers with the real thing and kernels-community landed batched-generation fixes. 

## Remove deprecated data helpers (#49360) huggingface/transformers 

 by Marc Sun 

The pre-`datasets` helpers (`GlueDataset`, `SquadDataset`, the GLUE/SQuAD/XNLI processors and metrics) are gone from `transformers.data.{datasets,processors,metrics}`, along with their top-level exports and dummy objects; the data collators and the slow GLUE evaluation set are unchanged. Marc Sun notes the helpers "have been deprecated for years and have had no users in the library since the le...

## Build real GOLD trainers in the on-policy generation tests huggingface/trl 

 by albertvillanova 

The GOLD on-policy generation tests now run against a real trainer with its real tokenizer and model instead of a `__new__`-built trainer, hand-written tokenizers and a scripted model. The stubs could not notice a change in trainer setup or in how a real tokenizer decodes special and pad tokens, so regressions in that path are now visible in CI.

## Build real GOLD VLM trainers in the on-policy generation tests huggingface/trl 

 by albertvillanova 

The same treatment for the GOLD vision-language generation tests, which previously skipped `__init__`, generated with a fake model, used placeholder image objects and patched `unwrap_model_for_generation` and `prepare_multimodal_messages`. Third in the set, alongside the input-preparation tests and the contributing-guide guidance on testing through the public API, all under the #7565 effort.

## weathernext2-banded-attention: follow torch's float32 matmul precision (TF32x3 on NVIDIA) huggingface/kernels-community 

 by Raymondlol 

The model-facing attention in weathernext2-banded-attention now follows PyTorch's float32 matmul setting rather than always using IEEE dots: `tf32x3` at default full precision on NVIDIA only, Triton's default TF32 when TF32 is allowed, and `ieee` on ROCm and XPU. The change was requested by the kernel's author in the corresponding Transformers thread.

## Update mlx-quantization-metal-kernels huggingface/kernels-community 

 by SunMarc 

Also in kernels-community: mlx-quantization-metal-kernels was synced with the latest MLX quantization ops, fixing errors in batched generation, and ggml-gated-delta-net fixed `delta_gates` for batched decode. In huggingface/kernels, the nix-builder added Torch 2.15.0rc3 support along with new Triton dependencies and cupti-python for Torch 2.15 on CUDA 13.4.

Hugging Face — the week in review · RepoJournal

# Transformers 5.18 ships Nemotron 3 diarization 

 By RepoJournal · composed from the cited sources · human-reviewed weekly · methodology 

 The release also clears deprecated Mamba and mask, cache, and rotary paths, while TRL drops vLLM 0.20.0 support. 

 218 commits 175 PRs merged 5 releases 7 briefings covered 

## Release 5.18.0 huggingface/transformers 

 by vasqu 

Nemotron 3 Diarization is an open-weight streaming speaker diarization model, released alongside the usual model additions in the 5.18.0 tag. It is a breaking release, so treat the version bump as a migration, not a drop-in.

## Seed before creating the model in experimental trainers huggingface/trl 

 by albertvillanova 

The experimental trainers build the PEFT model in __init__ before Trainer.__init__ calls set_seed, so LoRA adapters were getting whatever RNG state happened to be current. The trainer now seeds before creating the model, matching what the main trainers already do.

## Drop vLLM 0.20.0 support (#7435) huggingface/trl 

 by Quentin Gallouédec 

vLLM 0.20.0 is no longer supported, which lands as a hard floor for anyone running TRL's async or vLLM-backed trainers. Pin your vLLM version deliberately rather than inheriting whatever the environment resolves.

## Add selective activation checkpointing (SAC) to SFT huggingface/trl 

 by kashif 

With gradient checkpointing on, attention output is now saved during forward instead of recomputed in backward, recovering most of the checkpointing slowdown at long context for one extra hidden-state-sized tensor per layer.

## Deprecate opencode_env and pi_env in favour of harbor_env huggingface/OpenEnv 

 by sergiopaniego 

OpenCode and Pi are validated Harbor harnesses with the same token-level capture for training, so the per-harness envs duplicate an existing path. Both are removed in OpenEnv 0.8.0, which is your migration window if you reference opencode_env or pi_env.

## Deprecate the use_mamba_kernels config flag that no longer has any effect (#49155) huggingface/transformers 

 by Albert Villanova del Moral 

The flag stays accepted in configs but no longer has any effect, so existing configs will not break, they will just keep carrying a setting that does nothing.

## fix(setup): give xet-core duration defaults a unit so they apply huggingface/hf-mount 

 by XciD 

xet-core parses durations with humantime, which rejects a bare number and silently falls back to its own default with a WARN hidden by the default hf_mount=info filter. Two defaults set in init_tracing never applied as a result, so hf-mount users should recheck their duration settings.

## [MFU] Use device peak flops instead of hardcoded H100's huggingface/trl 

 by dwarez 

Async trainers computed MFU with the hardcoded H100 peak flops default; they now map peak flops by device, so the number reflects the hardware you actually ran on. Alongside: kernels removed the cxx11 ABI tag from Linux builds while keeping client-side parsing of tagged variants, funes now pulls unpushed local memory turns into recall and brings installed integrations forward on update, and Rep...

Hugging Face Transformers 5.18 Adds NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3 Diarization | AI.info

# Hugging Face Transformers 5.18 Adds NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3 Diarization

Hugging Face released Transformers 5.18.0 on September 30, adding support for NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3 Diarization model. The open-weight model identifies up to eight speakers and supports both streaming and offline audio processing.

AI.info Team · 2026-09-30

Hugging Face released Transformers 5.18.0 on September 30 with built-in support for NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3 Diarization, an open-weight model that tracks who speaks when. The integration lets developers load the model through the Transformers library’s standard audio-classification interfaces. It supports live, chunk-by-chunk processing as well as offline analysis of recorded audio.

## Eight speakers, one shared timeline

Nemotron 3 Diarization can identify as many as eight speakers, assigning speaker outputs according to the order each person first appears in the audio. That ordering is intended to keep speaker identities consistent as a conversation progresses. The model can process meetings, calls, podcasts and other conversational recordings, and can supply speaker labels and timestamps for speech-recognition systems.

The model uses an Arrival-Order Speaker Cache and a first-in, first-out queue to carry speaker information and recent audio context across streaming chunks. With chunked inference, the documentation says, the maximum recording duration is not limited. Output frame resolution can be configured in multiples of 10 milliseconds.

## What the latency figures mean

The release notes describe configurable input-buffer settings from 80 milliseconds up to a 30.4-second offline-style buffer. Those figures describe audio buffering, not the time a user necessarily waits for a result. The Transformers documentation lists streaming modes with audio-wait latencies of 1.04 seconds, 0.64 seconds and 0.32 seconds, excluding computation time.

The model card says the buffer can be set as low as 80 milliseconds, but identifies 0.32 seconds as the lowest recommended configuration. That distinction matters for applications that need quick speaker updates: the smallest available buffer setting is not the same as a recommended end-to-end latency target.

## Transformers makes the checkpoint easier to load

Developers can load the model with `AutoProcessor` and `AutoModelForAudioFrameClassification`, the general-purpose interfaces shown in the library’s examples. In streaming use, the processor splits audio into chunks, and the model returns a speaker cache that the next call can reuse. The final chunk is handled separately so the model can score remaining frames without look-ahead.

The NVIDIA model card lists the checkpoint at 99.2 million parameters and identifies its license as OpenMDW 1.1. The card says the model is intended for commercial or non-commercial use under that license. Transformers 5.18 adds library support; it does not introduce a new checkpoint or change the model’s license.

## A library integration, not a new model launch

NVIDIA’s model card gives September 23, 2026, as the model’s release date, a week before the Transformers update. The September 30 release therefore marks its addition to Hugging Face’s library, making the existing checkpoint accessible through a familiar loading and inference path. The release notes also list other model additions and software changes, but Nemotron 3 Diarization is the update’s notable audio-processing addition.

For developers, the practical change is direct access to streaming diarization in Transformers without building a separate integration around the checkpoint. The model’s speaker limit, chunk handling and latency settings define what that support provides: speaker-attributed audio frames, with buffer choices that trade faster updates against more context.
